opportunity: A call argument narrower than int that the caller zero-extends (movzx edi,di; movzbl) is trimmed to its narrow value, and C's integer promotion then widens the printed argument again: `sink(a0 * 3)` passes the untruncated product where the binary passes zext16(a0 * 3), and `sink(*(char *)(a0 + 3))` sign-extends a byte the binary zero-extends. Upstream Ghidra 12.1 prints the same `sink(param_1 * 3)`.
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-truncarg.xml (12 assertions; #1-#4 and #8 fail on main, #10 fails with c_range disabled, #11/#12 (clang forwarders) fail when the cast ignores the trim evidence) + tests/stages/kuna-endptrbound.xml #5 (legitimate change) + docs/features/truncarg/roundtrip/roundtrip.sh (compile-and-run, gcc and clang, NEW_WRONG against a base kuna)
change_kind: strict correctness fix (no option: it only restores the zero-extension the trim proved the binary performed)
root_cause: ActionDeadCode counts only minimalmask(nzmask) of an unlocked call input as consumed, so RDI = ZEXT(x & 0xffff) consumes 0xffff; RuleSubvarAnd's SubvariableFlow then trims the call input to the 2-byte value through tryCallPull (nothing outside the mask is consumed). ActionSetCasts' default getInputCast compares the unlocked parameter's local type (undefined2) with the argument and asks for no cast, so a sub-int arithmetic argument prints bare and C promotes it. Found with an instrumented throwaway build printing the p-code after every changing rule/action (subvar_and is the step that replaces CALL sink,RDI:8 with CALL sink,DI:2). For a byte the trim leaves TYPE_UNKNOWN, a second cause: upstream's localExtensionType treats TYPE_UNKNOWN as zero-extending, but realtypes prints a one-byte unknown as `char`, which C sign-extends, so the promotion check and the printed C disagreed. A narrow call input is not always such a trim: clang forwards a narrow parameter as the register it received (`mov %dil,acc8; jmp sinki`), where heritage gives the call a DIL:1 input from the start and no trim runs; nothing there says which extension the binary used.
fix: Evidence (P3): SubvariableFlow::try_call_pull notes a call slot whose trim drops only known-zero bits (kuna_truncarg::drops_only_zero_bits: the wide input's nzmask lies inside the logical mask anchored at bit 0); when the rewrite commits, do_replacement records (slot, new size, input count) on the call's FuncCallSpecs (note_trimmed_arg), and a trim without that proof clears the slot. Cast (P9): p9_emit/kuna_truncarg.rs (narrowed_arg_cast), consulted by the default getInputCast arm when cast_standard asks for nothing and only when the output language promotes (LangCaps::integer_promotion: C yes, Rust no): a recorded CALL/CALLIND input still at the recorded size and input count, narrower than sizeof(int), integer/unknown-typed and not an enum, whose slot no declared prototype type-locks, gets a cast to the unsigned integer of its width unless its promoted C value is already the zero-extension (int_promotion_type for an expression; the natural extension of the printed type for a variable, load or cast; a ZEXT always) or its C value provably lies in [0, 2^(8*size)) (c_range over sign-clear constants, truth values, + * & | ^, and variables whose def keeps the sign bit clear). The promotion check runs through FuncdataCastContext::with_unknown_byte_as, which reports a non-constant one-byte TYPE_UNKNOWN as int1 when ArchContext::unknown_byte_is_char (realtypes on, C output). An argument already printed as a truncating SUBPIECE cast, every read of which is a call argument, is retyped instead of double-cast (retype_truncation).

notes: The cast restores the zero-extension the trim removed: it fires only on a slot whose trim dropped known-zero bits. Inputs narrow for any other reason (a parameter clang forwards untouched, a sign-extension trimmed because the callee reads only the low bytes, a parameter recovered narrow) keep main's promoted form, which leaves clang's unsigned-char forwarder (r6) wrong exactly as on main: its bytes equal the signed one's. A `char` is cast even on targets whose char is unsigned (arm32): C leaves char's signedness to the implementation, and the cast is right under either. The redundant casts are the price of deciding at the call site without the callee's prototype; a locked prototype suppresses the cast (stage assertion #7). Still open, named in 09-emission.md: the same trim at the promotion width (`sink64(a0 * 3)` with int a0, trimmed from RDI = ZEXT(EDI)) is converted by C with sign extension against an 8-byte callee; casting there would touch nearly every int argument on x86-64.
